button_rules: For (a) a scam SMS, call, or WhatsApp message before any money is lost, make report_chakshu (Sanchar Saathi Chakshu at sancharsaathi.gov.in or the Sanchar Saathi app) the primary button—it is DoT's dedicated pre-loss channel for suspected fraud communications so scam numbers and headers get disconnected—with lost_money_1930 only as a secondary option if money was already sent, while report_cybercrime (cybercrime.gov.in) is primary only for non-financial cybercrimes like sextortion or blackmail. For (b) a message implying money was already taken or transferred (including an unexpected genuine bank debit alert), make lost_money_1930 (Call 1930, offline via ACTION_DIAL) the primary button for immediate golden-hour freezes, with report_cybercrime (cybercrime.gov.in, the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal for formal complaints and FIR follow-up) as secondary—not Chakshu, which explicitly directs financial-loss victims to 1930 and cybercrime.gov.in. For (c) a lookalike or phishing link, make report_chakshu primary when no money or credentials were given (Chakshu accepts phishing links and suspected fraud messages), keep lost_money_1930 secondary in case money was already debited, and use report_cybercrime for formal phishing or account-compromise complaints.
notes: 1930 misrouting on pre-loss calls/messages: 'Never stay on a video call with police; check by calling 1930.' treats 1930 as a police-verification line, and ACTIONS[1][2], 'a fake police or customs threat', and 'an extortion threat' direct users to 1930 without checking if money was lost. In India 2026, 1930 is strictly the financial cyber-fraud golden-hour helpline; pre-loss scam calls/SMS/WhatsApp belong on Sanchar Saathi Chakshu (sancharsaathi.gov.in / Sanchar Saathi app), non-financial cybercrime on cybercrime.gov.in (or 112 for physical threats), and 1930 only when money was transferred or debited.

Chakshu narrowed to 'SMS': 'Report the SMS on Sanchar Saathi Chakshu.' appears in 7 scam types (including 'an identity-document scam', whose first step explicitly says WhatsApp). Chakshu accepts calls, SMS, WhatsApp, and malicious links (within 30 days); saying 'the SMS' misleads WhatsApp and voice-call victims.

Remote-access app recovery risk: 'Freeze your cards in the bank app and call 1930.' immediately follows 'switch on airplane mode and uninstall it.' Opening the bank app on a potentially still-compromised phone (or turning data back on before uninstall finishes) is risky, and freezing cards alone does not stop UPI or netbanking theft; users should uninstall offline, then block cards, UPI, and netbanking from another device or the bank's card helpline, and call 1930 if money was debited.

Card-only containment for OTP/PIN/phishing: 'If you shared it, freeze your card in the bank app.' and 'If you entered card details, freeze the card in the bank app.' miss UPI PIN and netbanking credential theft, where freezing a card does not protect the account. The three phishing-link entries also omit any reporting step (Chakshu pre-loss, or 1930/cybercrime.gov.in if money was lost).

NPCI P2P UPI collect ban (India 2026): From 1 October 2025 (NPCI Circular NPCI/UPI/OC/220/2025-26), person-to-person (P2P) UPI collect requests were discontinued across India and merchant checkouts migrated heavily to QR/intent in 2026. 'Receiving money never needs a UPI PIN' remains vital, but India 2026 UPI scams rely mainly on merchant collect requests, UPI AutoPay mandates, and QR/intent links rather than P2P collect requests.

SEBI Check & @valid UPI handles (India 2026): 'Check the adviser or broker on SEBI's official website.' misses SEBI's October 2025 SEBI Check tool (siportal.sebi.gov.in / Saa₹thi app) and mandatory '@valid' UPI handles, which verify the actual receiving UPI ID or bank account and IFSC—important because scammers impersonate genuine SEBI-registered broker names with mule accounts.

Malicious APK gap: 'Do not install loan apps sent over chat.' lacks post-install damage control (revoke contacts/SMS/photo permissions, uninstall, report on cybercrime.gov.in and RBI Sachet sachet.rbi.org.in), and in India 2026 WhatsApp APK malware also targets KYC, electricity bill, and traffic e-Challan scams.

India Post app naming risk: 'Check any parcel charge in the India Post or courier app.' can nudge older users to search app stores or Google for 'India Post app' where fake APK/ad clones appear; India Post's official portal is indiapost.gov.in (its official app is named PostInfo).

Genuine debit/OTP alert gap: ACTIONS[0] ('Verify in the official app; never share your OTP or PIN.') is safe for benign promos/receipts, but for a genuine bank debit or OTP alert judged NO RISK FOUND, users also need an immediate unauthorised-payment step (provided in debit_alert_step) if they did not initiate the transaction.
